joshua.10.p1.b1.text: Now Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard … that the people of Gibeon had made peace with Israel … So Adoni-zedek and his people were greatly alarmed,

joshua.10.p1.b2.text: … sent word to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon,

joshua.10.p1.b3.text: “Come up and help me. We will attack Gibeon, because they have made peace with Joshua and the Israelites.”

joshua.10.p1.b4.text: So the five kings of the Amorites … joined forces and advanced with all their armies. They camped before Gibeon and made war against it.

joshua.10.p2.b1.text: “Do not abandon your servants. Come quickly and save us! Help us …

joshua.10.p2.b2.text: So Joshua and his whole army, including all the mighty men of valor, came from Gilgal.

joshua.10.p2.b3.text: “Do not be afraid of them, for I have delivered them into your hand. Not one of them shall stand against you.”

joshua.10.p3.b1.text: After marching all night from Gilgal,

joshua.10.p3.b3.text: And the LORD threw them into confusion before Israel, … pursued them along the ascent to Beth-horon, and struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

joshua.10.p4.b1.text: As they fled before Israel along the descent from Beth-horon to Azekah,

joshua.10.p4.b2.text: … the LORD cast down on them large hailstones from the sky,

joshua.10.p4.b3.text: … more of them were killed by the hailstones than by the swords of the Israelites.

joshua.10.p5.b1.text: On the day that the LORD gave the Amorites over to the Israelites, Joshua spoke to the LORD in the presence of Israel:

joshua.10.p5.b2.text: “O sun, stand still over Gibeon, O moon, over the Valley of Aijalon.”

joshua.10.p5.b3.text: So the sun stood still and the moon stopped until the nation took vengeance upon its enemies.

joshua.10.p5.b4.text: “So the sun stopped in the middle of the sky and delayed going down about a full day.” There has been no day like it before or since, when the LORD listened to the voice of a man, because the LORD fought for Israel.

joshua.10.p6.b1.text: Now the five kings had fled and hidden in the cave at Makkedah.

joshua.10.p6.b2.text: “The five kings have been found; they are hiding in the cave at Makkedah.”

joshua.10.p6.b3.text: “Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave, and post men there to guard them.

joshua.10.p7.b1.text: But you, do not stop there. Pursue your enemies … for the LORD your God has delivered them into your hand.”

joshua.10.p7.b2.text: … the remaining survivors retreated to the fortified cities.

joshua.10.p7.b3.text: The whole army returned safely to Joshua in the camp at Makkedah,

joshua.10.p7.b4.text: … no one dared to utter a word against the Israelites.

joshua.10.p8.b1.text: “Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me.”

joshua.10.p8.b2.text: … he summoned all the men of Israel and said to the army commanders who had accompanied him, “Come here and put your feet on the necks of these kings.”

joshua.10.p8.b4.text: “Be strong and courageous, for the LORD will do this to all the enemies you fight.”

joshua.10.p9.b2.text: At sunset Joshua ordered that they be taken down from the trees and thrown into the cave in which they had hidden.

joshua.10.p9.b3.text: Then large stones were placed against the mouth of the cave, and the stones are there to this day.

joshua.10.p10.b1.text: Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Makkedah to Libnah and fought against Libnah.

joshua.10.p10.b2.text: Joshua conquered the area from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and the whole region of Goshen as far as Gibeon.

joshua.10.p10.b3.text: And because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel, Joshua captured all these kings and their land in one campaign.

joshua.10.p10.b4.text: Then Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal.
